# Arctic sea ice extent on 2026-10-29 (NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4): research notes

## 1. Resolution source
- Daily values come from [N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv). My fetch tool truncates the file, so I read it in sections.
- 2026-10-07: the latest daily value I could get was **6.007 million km²**. I could not retrieve the 2026-10-08 row because the text was cut off at that point.
- 2026 values leading up to that, from the same file:
  - Sept 12 minimum: 4.574
  - Sept 20: 4.709
  - Sept 25: 5.169
  - Sept 30: 5.478
  - Oct 1: 5.650
  - Oct 3: 5.771
  - Oct 5: 5.860
  - Oct 6: 5.959
  - Oct 7: 6.007

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened yet that settles the question. Ice is in the fast autumn freeze-up. Since Sept 28 it has grown by about 0.05 to 0.1 million km² a day: from 5.333 on Sept 28 to 6.007 on Oct 7, which is 0.67 in 9 days.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-07: NSIDC's analysis "Stranger Things in the 2026 Arctic" says:
  - Freeze-up has been fast, and extent has reached the lower interdecile range of the record.
  - September averaged 4.81 million km², the 13th lowest on record.
  - Ice is still below average along the Eurasian coast, especially in the Kara and Barents Seas.
  - September air temperatures over the Arctic Ocean were 0 to 1 °C below average, but northern Eurasia was strongly above average.
  - [NSIDC](https://nsidc.org/sea-ice-today/analyses/stranger-things-2026-arctic)
- 2026-09-23: NSIDC put the preliminary minimum at 4.60 million km² on Sept 12 (a 5-day average). That ties 2008, 2010 and 2025 for 10th lowest. [NSIDC](https://nsidc.org/news-analyses/news-stories/arctic-sea-ice-has-reached-minimum-extent-2026-antarctic-sea-ice-maximum-most-likely-reached-well)
- NASA gives the same minimum, about 4.6 million km² on Sept 12. [NASA](https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/arctic-sea-ice-shrinks-to-its-2026-minimum/)

## 4. Base rates
Daily values from the v4 file. The last column is the gain from Oct 8 to Oct 29.

| Year | Oct 5 | Oct 8 | Oct 29 | Gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2018 | n/a | 5.161 | 7.705 | +2.54 |
| 2019 | n/a | 4.963 | 7.427 | +2.46 |
| 2020 | n/a | 4.721 | 6.526 | +1.81 |
| 2021 | n/a | 5.802 | 8.301 | +2.50 |
| 2022 | 5.551 | 5.659 | 8.305 | +2.65 |
| 2023 | 5.087 | 5.296 | 8.216 | +2.92 |
| 2024 | 4.870 | 4.917 | 7.563 | +2.65 |
| 2025 | n/a | 5.728 | 7.629 | +1.90 |

- The Oct 8 to Oct 29 gain over 2018 to 2025 averaged about +2.43, with a range of +1.81 to +2.92 and a standard deviation of about 0.37. The smallest gains came in 2020, when the Laptev freeze-up was delayed, and in 2025.
- Measured from Oct 5 instead, the gain to Oct 29 was +2.75 (2022), +3.13 (2023) and +2.69 (2024).
- **2026 is running above every year from 2018 to 2025 for early October**:
  - Oct 5, 2026 was 5.860, compared with 5.551 in 2022, the highest of the 2022 to 2024 Oct 5 values above.
  - Oct 7, 2026 was 6.007, compared with 5.802 for 2021 on Oct 8.
- My own arithmetic, not a forecast: adding those historical gains to roughly 6.05 to 6.10 on Oct 8 would give about 7.9 to 9.0, with a central value near 8.5.
- Other data points:
  - 2025: Sept daily minimum 4.543, Oct 30 was 7.686, Oct 31 was 7.676.
  - Oct 31 values: 2022 was 8.539, 2023 was 8.478, 2024 was 7.637.
  - [NSIDC file](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- Day-to-day noise in the daily series is often ±0.05 to 0.1, and occasionally a single-day jump of ±0.15 or more (for example Sept 15 to 16, 2026 went from 4.724 to 4.656).

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market or expert forecast for the Oct 29 daily extent.
- Polymarket and Kalshi ran markets on the 2026 summer minimum, using the NSIDC daily minimum between Aug 1 and Oct 1. Those closed on Oct 1 and don't apply here. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/prismatic/which-arctic-sea-ice-minimum-thresh), [Orrery](https://orrery.me/markets/will-the-minimum-arctic-sea-ice-extent-this-summer-be-at-least-5m-square-kilometers)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- NSIDC usually publishes a Sea Ice Today update in mid-October and an October summary in early November.
- Main sources of uncertainty:
  - How fast the Kara, Barents and Laptev Seas freeze. They were below average in early October.
  - Hudson Bay and the Chukchi Sea, which usually start freezing in late October to November.
  - Warm air over northern Eurasia (above average in September per NSIDC) could slow freezing on the Atlantic and Eurasian side.
- I could not find an official weather or sea ice outlook for Oct 8 to 29.
- Data caveat: the near-real-time NSIDC values can be revised slightly, and occasional missing or bad satellite days get filled.
